methodologyNotes: Roster covers 14 outdoor flat-top gas griddle models spanning entry-level tabletops through premium freestanding units from Blackstone, Weber, Camp Chef, Pit Boss, Royal Gourmet, Nexgrill, LoCo Cookers, and Halo. Sources are official manufacturer product pages (blackstoneproducts.com, weber.com, campchef.com, pitboss-grills.com, royalgourmetusa.com, nexgrill.com, halocooks.com/atbbq.com, lococookers.com) plus major retailers (Walmart, Amazon, Home Depot, BBQGuys, Lowe's, Bass Pro, Sportsman's). prices are the lowest published US MSRP or list/sale price found on a manufacturer or major-retail page at access time; where the manufacturer site was offline (LoCo) or the SKU varies by retailer (Nexgrill 720-1058A), the corroborating retailer listing for the EXACT named SKU was used. cooking_area_sqin is primary griddle surface only; side_shelves is a boolean (true = at least one folding or fixed prep shelf; a swing-away warming rack alone = false); cooktop_material uses the manufacturer's own description; accessedAt 2026-06-19. Adversarial pass corrected the Royal Gourmet price (no support for $269.99; official current price is $319.99), corrected Halo Elite4B fuel from dual_fuel to propane (the natural-gas conversion kit HZ-3001-B ships separately, the unit ships propane), repointed the Nexgrill source to the verified 720-1058A listing (the brand 'with lid' page is a different 38,000 BTU / 532 sqin variant), repointed the Camp Chef FTG600 source from a promo 'no grill grates' SKU to the standard FTG600 listing, and fixed the Blackstone 36 cooking area from 769 to the official 768 sqin.

products.name: Traeger Flatrock 3-Zone Flat Top Griddle (TF3CN59AU)
products.priceNote: Traeger.com list price $999.99 for the Flatrock 3 Zone (TF3CN59AU); Texas Star Grill Shop lists regular $999.95 / sale $899.99.
products.provenance: Traeger.com official Flatrock page confirmed the 3 Zone model (TF3CN59AU) at $999.99: total cooking area 594 sq in on a 33" x 18" cooktop, 47K BTUs/hr on high, "Triple U-burner design" (three U-shaped burners) with three insulated TruZone cooking zones, a cold-rolled steel recessed surface, and built-in folding side shelves. The page's FAQ states "use liquid propane only" (no natural gas), and specifies the 3 Zone has an electric ignitor that runs off a 9-volt battery or plug-in — establishing propane fuel and electric ignition. Texas Star Grill Shop (an authorized Traeger retailer) corroborated the exact SKU TF3CN59AU as the Flatrock 3-Zone propane griddle with foldable P.A.L.-rail shelves and flame sensors. No release year is stated on either fetched page, so release and releaseDate are left null rather than guessed. Re-fetch 2026-07-10 confirmed every non-null spec value verbatim.

products.name: Solo Stove Steelfire 22" Stainless Griddle (SS22-G-UNIT)
products.priceNote: Tom's Guide hands-on review (published 2 June 2026) states "The Solo Stove Steelfire 22 Griddle is priced at $400" and lists "Price: $400" in its spec box. The Amazon Solo Stove Store listing (ASIN B0H42SRNRZ) returned an anti-bot interstitial ("Continue shopping") with no product or pricing data at access, so the $400 figure is sourced entirely from Tom's Guide (stated US MSRP, available on solostove.com).
products.provenance: The Amazon source listing (ASIN B0H42SRNRZ) returned an anti-bot interstitial page with no product data on re-fetch, and Solo Stove's own manufacturer page returned HTTP 403, so no spec could be verified from either the source URL or the manufacturer. Every retained value is instead corroborated verbatim by the Tom's Guide hands-on review: price $400; a single racetrack burner ("the 22 only has one," with "a single control knob," vs two racetrack burners on the larger Steelfire 30); 14,000 BTU burner power; 321.7 square-inch cooking surface; a cooktop "made from triple-layer clad stainless steel"; propane fuel (designed for 1-pound tanks); and an "integrated starter" for ignition. side_shelves is null because neither fetched page states the presence or absence of a prep/side shelf. release/releaseDate are null because no fetched page states a release date — the review's 2 June 2026 publication date is not an explicit product release. Unverifiable Amazon-only details asserted in the original entry (UPC 810167605754, a "21.75 in by 16.5 in" surface breakdown, "patent-pending" burner language) were dropped from provenance since the Amazon page could not be fetched; only spec values independently confirmed by Tom's Guide are retained.

Re-verified 2026-07-10: all six non-null spec values, priceUsd, and releaseDate explicitly supported by fetched text; exact model HZ-1002-XNA confirmed (not the sibling Elite4B, a distinct $1,099.99 four-burner product).
